verdicts.reason: The report prints a stored expected value instead of reading the game, so it misses a changed health value. Both are listed false passes and red outcomes.
The sky must be rainless. A supposed dry storm that rains is the named red outcome.
The untouched site shows mineral flora and fauna, distinct soils, a lightning sky without rain and five distinct weather states at play zoom.
The hazardous pool becomes fresh water at the pump boundary. This is an explicit false pass and red outcome.
The cue starts after harmful exposure. The lull must come about one in-game hour before bloom and before the dose.

Visible lull and stillness from eligible idle natives come about 2500 ticks before bloom, a sleeping native is correctly excluded, the optional message is not required, and the worker reaches shelter before the dose.
A fully sealed worker accumulates ambient metal dose while the item survives. This is the named false pass and red outcome.
The exposed control is harmed and roofed and fully sealed workers keep their starting health. The helmet-only worker follows the partial-equipment rule.
Metal clears on its own. A slow natural decay labelled permanent is an explicit false pass.
A low saved trace is purged by a normal advanced health bill with ingredient use and operation completion.
The acid sensory injury heals away and capacity returns to baseline, so no permanent disfigurement or sensory damage remains.
A completed harvest pays no metal and the payout does not follow the assay. This is the named red outcome.
Three seed-bearing bound rhossak resting together root a young thornwood. Galled animals bind, drop edible galls and remain seedless.
A ranged hit on a suush must start a toxic detonation. A shot suush that simply dies is the red outcome.
Lined taps must resist prying. Pry damage to a lined tap is the red outcome.
Wild drinking suppresses the tap and output recovers afterwards. Shearing a tame animal supplies vexxith without killing it.
Sealed diagonal barriers must stop the chain. Leaking through a sealed corner is the red outcome.
A dramatic blast that throws none of the identified goods is the red outcome.
Work must pause without losing stock when power is missing. Input vanishing with no product is silent stock loss.
All-off must not cure lasting health or destroy stock. Erasing poisoned pawns' hediffs or banked liquids is an explicit false pass.
Prepared workers complete routine work without ambient injury and stock reconciles. The exposed expedition and wild vexxiss still present risk.
Reload must preserve grove bindings. Losing bound trees on reload is the named red outcome.
Poisoning clears without advanced treatment. Slow natural decay presented as persistent is an explicit false pass.
Sensory capacity returns to its original value. A scar label without lasting sensory loss fails the sensory-organ requirement.
The visible vent and animal cues must give about one hour. The optional message only supplements those cues and cannot replace them.
A roof must protect against both ambient bloom and acid. Roof protection working for only one ambient route is the red outcome.
Straight and diagonal sealed barriers must both stop the chain. The flame leaks through the sealed corner.
Goods destroyed and respawned elsewhere with new ids is an explicit false pass. The identified goods must be thrown.
All-off must not cure lasting health, and re-enable must resume coherently. The poisoning was erased.
Metal must scale with growth and follow the assay. The young tree pays the same 12 steel as the mature tree despite its lower assay.

ambiguities: e11: the leaf says acid 'can' leave permanent harm, shown across a finite batch. One healed case alone may not prove impossibility, but the scenario shows the sensory injury fully restoring, so it was judged against the leaf.
